messages:
security-bot: [asset-indexer] detected gs://redwood-metadata-exports as LISTABLE by public indexer. sample event: storage.objects.list, principal=allUsers, first-seen=2026-03-20T10:12:34Z. tagging eng-security.
maya: ack - looking. can someone confirm whether artifacts are in that bucket or just metadata dumps?
sam: I can take emergency lock. running quick check now.
alex: FYI that bucket is created by the metadata-export pipeline (daily). it used to be private; last terraform change was 2026-03-10 by infra-deploy-bot.
nina: I see a recent manual gsutil ACL change in audit logs at 2026-03-20T09:58:10Z by serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood. looks like an accidental role binding applied.
maya: containment plan: 1) immediate deny public list access 2) rotate any keys that had broad access 3) audit objects read in last 24h 4) follow up RBAC fix in terraform.
sam: emergency commands I'm running now (will paste output):
```
# block public access (GCS)
gsutil iam ch -d allUsers:objectViewer gs://redwood-metadata-exports || true
# also set uniform bucket-level access
gsutil uniformbucketlevelaccess set on gs://redwood-metadata-exports
# quick policy to deny public
gcloud storage buckets update gs://redwood-metadata-exports --no-website --public-access-prevention enforced
```
sam: command output: applied public-access-prevention=ENFORCED, uniform access enabled. previous ACL entries removed: allUsers:READER.
ops-oncall: good containment. next: check who read objects while public.
maya: querying audit logs for storage.objects.get/list where resource=redwood-metadata-exports and protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail is null or principal=allUsers.
```
# BigQuery export path (example)
SELECT
  protoPayload.methodName, protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, timestamp
FROM `project.logging.cloudaudit_googleapis_com_data_access_*`
WHERE resource.labels.bucket_name = 'redwood-metadata-exports'
  AND timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 24 HOUR)
```
maya: preliminary: saw ~12 list requests from 8 unique IPs attributed to anonymous indexers between 09:45 and 10:05 UTC. no large object GETs observed yet, mostly LIST.
alex: that suggests metadata scrape rather than artifact download. still a breach of exposure triangle.
nina: serviceAccount ci-runner had roles/storage.objectAdmin bound by a broad IAM binding in project infra-automation at 2026-03-10. recommending to remove broad binding and grant least-privilege.
maya: agreed. immediate RBAC action: remove role binding, create scoped role for the pipeline with only needed perms (objects.create, objects.delete for prefix), and update terraform.
sam: opened PR to revert manual change and add guard: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/2345 - marked as emergency. will push apply after approvals if no objections.
ops-oncall: also recommend rotating any credentials associated with the pipeline SA and restricting KMS decrypt to specific service accounts. check CMEK key policy.
alex: current KMS key policy allows project editors to decrypt. that's too broad. I'll prepare minimal key policy: only ci-runner-sa and storage-service-sa can decrypt, plus security-serviceaccount for audits.
maya: also add logs pipeline rule to alert on public ACL changes and enforce terraform-only changes via policy (deny non-terraform ACL writes).
ops-oncall: filing incident ticket INC-2026-0893 and notifying legal/compliance. I'll post to #incidents after we have containment status.
security-bot: incident ticket created INC-2026-0893. slack notification sent to #incidents and #product-security.
nina: post-incident actions suggested:
- rotate and restrict SA keys used by pipeline
- tighten KMS key policy and rotate CMEK
- add terraform pre-commit checks to block allUsers ACLs
- add runtime alert for bucket public listing + auto-remediation (enforce public-access-prevention)
- run full object inventory and hash check for unexpected objects
- retro with infra team + update runbook
maya: assigning owners: sam for emergency bucket lock and terraform revert, alex for KMS policy, nina for SA key rotation and IAM least-privilege, maya to lead post-incident retro.
sam: applied emergency terraform change and will wait 5m to confirm no traffic regressions then merge.
alex: posted KMS policy PR https://git.internal/r/redwood/security/+/678 - please review.
nina: rotated pipeline SA keys and updated CI to use new short-lived token flow. removed broad role bindings.
maya: final checks: audit log scan completed for 24h window, no object GETs from anonymous principals, only LIST. marking containment=complete. moving to post-incident tasks.
ops-oncall: will schedule incident writeup and notify customer-facing teams if we need to communicate externally. closing emergency thread here, follow-ups in the incident ticket.
maya: thanks all. action items in INC-2026-0893. :thumbsup:
